recentItems.title: I spent years as Lebron James—then I became myself | Sheldon Bailey | TEDxManhattanBeach
recentItems.description:
For years, Sheldon Bailey was visible on set but invisible on screen—serving as the body double for NBA superstars like LeBron James and Shaquille O’Neal while chasing his own dreams of greatness. Through injury, rejection, and life in the shadows, he learned that identity is not defined by roles others assign you. This talk is a powerful reflection on stepping out of the background, owning your talent, and expecting your greatness. 

Sheldon “Big Shel” Bailey is redefining what it means to be multidimensional in a world that demands specialization. At 6’6”, he moves seamlessly between elite athletics, entertainment, and creative entrepreneurship—proving range is a strength. Bailey excelled in basketball, football, volleyball, Aussie Rules Football, and boxing, earning Division I scholarships to Winthrop University and Florida International University. While competing at the highest levels, he served as President of the Black Student Union and emerged as a spoken word poet. He has built a steady career across Netflix, Showtime, FX/Hulu, Nickelodeon, Amazon Prime, and Peacock, earning praise as “a standout” for his role as DeAndre Jordan in *Clipped*. A creative entrepreneur, Bailey has released three music projects, authored *180 Degrees*, produced the award-winning pilot *Adulting*, consults for major retail brands, and supports charities including St. Anne’s Today, The Salvation Army, and SOS Children’s Villages. 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The dark future of AI in war | Stephanie Hare | TEDxBerlin
recentItems.description:
Lethal autonomous weapon systems operate without a 'human in the loop', so who can we hold to account if they are ever used to kill humans?  Dr. Stephanie Hare, co-presenter of the BBC television programme AI Decoded, demonstrates how technology is not neutral, because there is always a human in the loop. Her conclusion: AI can't be put on trial for war crimes, but humans can — and should. Dr. Stephanie Hare is a researcher, broadcaster and author focused on technology, politics and history. 

She co-presents “Artificial Intelligence: Decoded” on BBC television and contributes to the BBC World Service.

Her first book, Technology Is Not Neutral: A Short Guide to Technology Ethics, was named a Financial Times Best Technology Book of summer 2022, and her writing has featured in the Financial Times, The Washington Post, the Guardian/Observer, the Harvard Business Review, WIRED and Computer Weekly. 

She has worked at Accenture, Palantir, and Oxford Analytica; held the Alistair Horne Visiting Fellowship at St Antony’s College, Oxford; and earned a PhD and MSc from the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) and a BA from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, including a year at the Université de la Sorbonne (Paris IV). 

This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: When love lasts eternally: A Portuguese love story | Miguel Júdice | TEDxMarvila
recentItems.description: There's a fountain on Miguel Júdice's family estate in Coimbra that thousands of people visit every year to celebrate eternal love — and he opens his talk by explaining why. It's the true story of his ancestors, Prince Pedro and Inês de Castro: a 14th-century romance forbidden by a king, ended by an assassination, and then, unbelievably, continued after death — Pedro exhumed her body, crowned her queen, and built their tombs foot to foot so they'd see each other first on judgment day. He tells it with real detail and real stakes, then turns it on the audience, asking what a swipe-left culture of situationships might learn from two people who chose each other completely, even past the point of reason. By the end, he leaves you with a challenge simple enough to actually act on: do one meaningful thing for someone you love, today. Come for the history — stay for where he takes it. Miguel Júdice is a hospitality entrepreneur with extensive experience in Portugal's luxury sector. His projects include the Hotel Quinta das Lágrimas, part of Small Luxury Hotels of the World, and Eleven Restaurant, awarded one Michelin star. He has led and advised numerous ventures across hospitality, real estate, and culture, and served as President of the Portuguese Hotel Association. Miguel holds a degree in Business from Universidade Católica Portuguesa and a Master's in Hospitality Management from Cornell University. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: How does the clumsy bird fly? | Polina Bibchenko | TEDxBHI
recentItems.description: Through choir, a solo singing competition, and internship applications, Polina learned that confidence comes after action. Her lesson: don’t wait to feel ready—and never give up. Polina Bibchenko is an outstanding graduate of Beijing Hospitality Institute (BHI) and currently a master’s student at Peking University HSBC Business School. She is a speaker at TEDxBHI. Through choir, a solo singing competition, a coffee-making course, and internship applications, she learned that confidence is not a prerequisite for action. Growth begins when we act before we feel ready. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The Five Rules of Love | Dan Whitlam | TEDxMarvila
recentItems.description: Dan Whitlam opens his talk with a line written for someone who doesn't exist yet, then spends the next few minutes being unusually honest about what he's learned about love the hard way — how the way we were held as children becomes the blueprint for how we love as adults, why intimacy is less about touch and more about actually being known, why the friends who've seen every bad version of you and stuck around anyway might be the purest example of love there is. It's a spoken-word set, but it doesn't feel like a performance so much as someone telling you the truth — watch it, and see which of his five rules you didn't know you needed to hear. Dan Whitlam is a poet, rapper, and musician whose work blends reflection, honesty, and emotional depth. After losing his mother young and surviving a stabbing at sixteen, he turned resilience into purpose — using music and poetry to inspire healing and connection. Fresh from his biggest headline tour across North America, Europe, and the UK, and with his debut album coming in 2026, Dan also supports mental-health charities like CALM and Kooth UK. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Shifting Perspectives on Research | Daniel Alland | TEDxNewark Academy
recentItems.description: This speaker examines the power of focused social interactions in shifting your perspectives, allowing you to see concepts differently in a way that can greatly improve your ability to do authentic research. Daniel Alland is an entrepreneur currently in his Junior year at Newark Academy. In his free time, he enjoys rock climbing, running, and designing ideas either for fun or as ideas for his next business. Daniel is also a leader in the Outdoors Club and a member of the student AI committee at NA. Daniel values understanding a wide range of ideas and understands that innovation involves making connections between people and between concepts. In his TedX talk, Daniel shares one technique he uses to gain understanding when making these connections. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Unstoppable: The Code of the Entrepreneurial Mindset | Cecilia Jauregui | TEDxUnivalle La Paz
recentItems.description:
This talk explores the beliefs, attitudes, and behaviors that enable people to become proactive creators of opportunities rather than passive observers of circumstances. The talk challenges the traditional idea that entrepreneurship begins with an idea, capital, or a business plan. Instead, it proposes that entrepreneurship begins with a decision: to think differently and take responsibility for creating the future.

Through practical insights and real-world examples, the talk introduces the essential elements of an entrepreneurial mindset vision, action, resilience, innovation, discipline, adaptability, and purpose and shows how these principles can be applied not only to business, but also to education, professional careers, and everyday life. Cecilia María Jáuregui Gamarra is a Bolivian industrial engineer, entrepreneur, and environmental leader. She is the founder and General Manager of INNOVAPLAST, an ecological plastics company based in El Alto, La Paz, focused on recycling plastic waste and developing environmentally friendly products.

Cecilia began her entrepreneurial journey at the age of 24, entering an industry traditionally dominated by men. Through perseverance, innovation, and a strong commitment to sustainability, she built INNOVAPLAST into a company recognized for promoting recycling, circular economy, and environmental responsibility.

Her work goes beyond environmental protection. INNOVAPLAST has developed initiatives that support and empower women recyclers by providing training and promoting fairer recognition of their work within the recycling chain. The company has been described as a triple-impact business, combining economic activity with social and environmental impact. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Humanity and humility in children’s heart surgery | José I. G. Fragata | TEDxMarvila
recentItems.description: "What's the difference between a cardiac surgeon and God?" Professor José Fragata opens with the punchline: "God does not think he is a cardiac surgeon." It's the first laugh in a talk built on forty years and nearly 4,000 operations on hearts no bigger than a walnut. But the real turning point is personal — early in his career, he and his wife learned their own daughter needed heart surgery. She's in the audience today, alive and well. From that moment on, he says, he understood the twin values that define his work: humanity and humility, "two faces of the same coin." Watch to hear the moment he shows a blue newborn his own pink fingernails for the first time — and why he believes you can cure a patient with technology, but it takes a human heart to heal one. Professor José Fragata is a distinguished academic cardiothoracic surgeon, former head of department, and full professor of surgery, now retired. His career spans more than 45 years, during which he performed thousands of cardiac procedures, including numerous heart and lung transplantations in both adults and children. He has an extensive and diverse body of published work and has held leading roles in several prominent international professional societies. Professor Fragata can be characterized by three defining qualities: perseverance, empathy, and professionalism. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Do-Re-Mi | Avicenna Orchestra | TEDxAvicenna Cinere School
recentItems.description:
For TEDx Avicenna Cinere School, themed “UNSEEN,” AVChestra presents one of the most iconic songs from the musical film The Sound of Music, “Do-Re-Mi." 

Rather than simply reproducing the original arrangement, this performance reflects the spirit of exploration that AVChestra seeks to nurture. Through the process of studying, adapting and developing the arrangement, students experience how a familiar piece of music can be transformed into something new through their collective effort and musical understanding. Avicenna Orchestra, officially abbreviated as AVChestra is a student orchestra and a creative space for musical exploration and artistic development at SMP Avicenna Cinere. Established in 2024, AVChestra empowers students not only to perform music, but also to learn, experiment, collaborate, and take an active role in the creative process behind each musical performance. Through this experience, students are encouraged to be proactive, joyful and confident in exploring their musical potential.

AVChestra was created with the vision of bringing an orchestra into the Avicenna community while opening new opportunities for students to discover and develop their musical potential. Since its formation, AVChestra has encouraged students to become more proactive and independent in learning music, including exploring musical arrangements, understanding different instruments and discovering how individual parts can come together to create a complete musical piece. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Quantum Chess: A New Lens on Uncertainty | Surya Raghavan | TEDxNewark Academy
recentItems.description: This speaker shares his experiences with the world’s most popular board game—chess—with a little twist. By bridging principles of quantum mechanics with the game he loves, Surya will explore how Quantum Chess reshaped his approach to uncertainty, decision-making, and life itself. Surya, a sophomore at Newark Academy, is passionate about many areas of STEM, with math at the heart of everything he does, alongside a deep interest in physics and computer science. As a competitive math student, he has participated in numerous national and international math tournaments, continuously pushing himself at the highest level. He is deeply committed to giving back, whether through volunteering as a math tutor with the OneInMath Program, raising funds for homeless youth, or brightening lives through Color A Smile. Outside of academics, he performs with the New Jersey Youth Symphony's Youth Orchestra and competes on NA's Varsity Swim team. Surya is excited to bring his passion for math and emerging technology to his TEDx talk, where he will explore how embracing uncertainty can help us all thrive in the upcoming quantum era. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Love and Gastronomy: Union or Ambivalence? | Suzana Barros | TEDxMarvila
recentItems.description: Is sharing a meal ever just eating? Restaurateur Suzana Barros doesn't think so. From a Portuguese painting of two lovers lost in conversation over dinner, to her childhood table set every night by candlelight, to the first-date jitters and quiet business deals she watches unfold nightly at her Lisbon restaurant Tágide — she makes the case that every meal carries something invisible: care, memory, belonging. But she doesn't stop at comfort. Drawing on centuries of art history, from tender family scenes to a 16th-century painting of hell itself, she shows how the same table that nourishes love has also hosted excess, power, even poison. So what is food, really — care, power, love, or something more dangerous? Watch to find out why Barros believes the answer isn't fixed. It's a choice we make every time we sit down. Suzana Barros is an art expert, entrepreneur, restaurateur, and ceramist whose work bridges creativity, culture, and community. With degrees from ESAD and Sotheby's Institute of Art, she began her career managing Portugal's artistic heritage at Millennium BCP before earning a master's in Strategic Marketing from ISCEM. For the past 18 years, Suzana has led Lisbon's iconic Tágide Restaurant and Tágide WG Bar, where gastronomy meets art and history. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: The beauty of yellow spot | Jinbao Wang | TEDxBHI
recentItems.description: Growing up between Beijing and Henan, Wang Jinbao felt he belonged nowhere—too “Henan” for Beijing, too “Beijing” for Henan. His mixed accent became a source of shame. Through stamp collecting, he discovered that flaws can make something valuable. His talk is about embracing your accent, your story, and your true self. You don’t need perfect English or a perfect life to be heard—you just need to be real. TEDxBHI speaker, studnet of BHI This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
